en: The Ritual for the Recitation of the Greatly Efficacious and Accomplished King of Holy Yamāntaka’s Wrathful Power, in One Scroll.
By the Grand Master of the Household, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra, Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, who was Duke of Suguang with a fief of three thousand households, invested with purple robes, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and given the title Dajian (Great Mirror) and the epithet Dayangzhi (Great and Vast Wisdom), by imperial decree. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha...
Observing the various bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings in the palaces of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens,
they addressed Mañjuśrī, saying: "In the past,
there were ten *asaṃkhyeya-koti* Tathāgatas."
They all, before the great sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva,
gave rise to the mind of unsurpassed bodhi and expounded the teachings and mantras of Mañjuśrī.
Desiring that the Buddha-dharma remain long in the world,
he empowered the king to protect the realm and to transform and guide sentient beings through the ten wholesome dharmas.
Now is the very time for you to proclaim it:
the Noble King Yamāntaka, in his wrathful form,
mounted upon a blue water buffalo and wielding various weapons.
He wears a necklace of skulls,
has a tiger-skin crown, and a loincloth;
his body is tall.
He was many immeasurable yojanas in height;
flames blazed from his entire body like the conflagration at the end of an eon,
and he gazed in the four directions with the majestic stride of a lion.
The supreme root mantra is spoken as follows:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām* | *apratihataśāsānām* | *oṃ kara kara kuru kuru mama kāryaṃ* ||1||
Bhañja bhañja | Sarvavighnān | Noha noha | Sarvavajravināyakān | Muruḍaṭaka | Irividantakarāla | Mahāvikṛtarūpiṇe || 12 ||

Maṇḍalamāte (27) praveśaya (28) samayam anu smarā (29) hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ sphoṭa sphoṭa svāhā. As soon as this mantra is recited...
The trichiliocosm shook in six ways.
All the celestial Māras and Vināyakas who create obstacles in the world found their palaces trembling violently, becoming terrified and unsettled.
They all gathered like clouds, prostrated before the Honored One of Great Majestic Power, and said:
"We pray only that you will have compassion for us and grant us fearlessness.
At that time, King Krodharāja addressed the Buddha, saying:
Regarding the mantras I have now spoken:
even a Bodhisattva of the Tenth Stage who hears these mantras and does not yet accord with the teachings will still be able to dissolve [their obstacles].
How much more so for other gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings who create obstacles and difficulties.
If one first recites this mantra ten thousand times,
one will then be able to perform various fierce and powerful methods of subjugation.
If there are wicked people or enemies who harbor malicious intentions toward virtuous persons and seek to harm them,
one should cast an image of the Wrathful King out of gold or copper, its dimensions being as large or small as desired.
In a clean room, construct a triangular altar and place an image upon it.
At the base of the altar,
draw the figure of that person or write down their name.
The image faces north.
The practitioner, dressed in black robes,
sits facing south.
Forming the spear-seal (*śakti-mudrā*) and uttering the wrathful incantation with a fierce voice,
one should recite it three times daily for seven days.
That evil person will either suffer from a malignant disease, be afflicted by a malignant ulcer, or their body will perish.
Furthermore, there is another method: draw that Śatadru on birch bark or palm leaves.
Once the drawing is finished, form the spear mudrā, press it upon his heart, and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times to empower it.
Thereafter, place the image in its seat.
Perform the ritual at noon on a day when the planet Mars is prominent.
Furthermore, perform it every day at midnight.
Press the śakti-mudrā upon the heart of that image and recite the mantra twenty-one times,
while visualizing that Śatru resides beneath the image.
Furthermore, his attendants and kinsmen will all perish.
Moreover, according to the ritual, one should first draw a triangular mandala;
within the mandala, one should draw the form of Śatru.
Carve stakes from khadira wood, each four inches in length,
with the tips shaped like a single-pronged trident.
Empower them by reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Insert the person's name into the phrase and add it beneath this line; thus,
it shall be driven into their heart.
For one month, recite the mantra three times each day before the image,
performing one hundred and eight recitations for each session.
Make offerings according to your means and burn agalloch incense.
When one month has passed, if the *dharu* is set up, the practitioner will become restless while sitting or lying down and flee far away;
later, they will suffer physical ailments until death.
The reciter should then give rise to compassion.
The method for performing the *śāntika* homa remains as previously described.
Next, the method for the Great Heart Mantra (*mahācitta-mantra*) is explained;
the mantra is as follows: Oṃ hrīḥ śrīḥ vikṛtānana hūṃ sarvaduṣṭān āśāpaya saṃpādaya saṃpādaya sphoṭaya sphoṭaya svāhā. Before the image of the Great Sage, one should construct a triangular mandala.
Recite this mantra ten thousand times;
once the meritorious practice is accomplished,
one should then take black mud.
Fashion it into the shape of a *śatru* (enemy) and lay it on its back.
Place donkey dung inside its belly.
Furthermore, take five donkey bones and fashion them into stakes, each six inches long.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over each stake individually.
Drive two stakes into the left and right shoulders,
and two stakes into the two thighs.
Fixing [the image] upon one's heart,
sit facing south and burn agalloch incense;
recite the mantra ten thousand times.
Upon his abandonment of the *dharu*, he immediately fell ill, spat blood, and died.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one constructs a triangular fire altar before the image and performs *homā* for seven nights.
Light a fire with thorns and brushwood.
Take leaves of the *kaṭuka-śālmali* tree and write the names of two people who love each other upon them,
placing the leaves back-to-back.
Wrap it in snake skin and bind the leaves with a cord made of weasel fur;
use one hundred and eight pieces.
Within the mantra phrases, one should utter the names of those two individuals.
Reciting the mantra once for each throw into the fire,
the two shall immediately come to hate and dislike one another, becoming discordant.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause evil persons to distance themselves from the Dharma,
take one hundred and eight feathers from a crow and burn them in a triangular furnace, having first soaked them in mustard oil.
Light a fire with thorny branches and perform a homa for one night,
reciting the person's name within the mantra syllables.
Recite [the mantra] once and cast it into the fire;
that person will immediately depart for a distant place of their own accord.
Furthermore, there is a method for seeking victory over enemy armies.
Take one hundred and eight blades of *kuśa* grass,
each twelve finger-widths long.
Dip them in sesame oil and burn them in a triangular hearth using thorny wood for fuel.
Perform the homa for seven nights,
reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times,
while invoking the name of that general within the phrases of the mantra.
Recite [the mantra] once and cast it into the fire;
immediately the enemy's military array will be shattered and victory shall be attained.
Furthermore, there is another method: take six *liang* of iron filings.
While reciting the mantra, call out the person's name. Then,
take a pinch [of the substance], empower it with the mantra,
and cast it into the triangular hearth one by one for each recitation.
Perform the homa for seven nights;
then, if he sets eyes upon it, he will immediately perish.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a khaṭvāṅga-wood stake four finger-widths long.
Within a triangular mandala,
draw the form of Śatru using charnel ground ashes;
recite the mantra one hundred and eight times to empower it.
Nail him down upon the heart of Śatru;
visualize yourself as the Great Majestic Wrathful Deity,
treading with your left foot upon the heart of Śatru.
Recite the mantra one thousand times,
inserting the person's name within the mantra;
that person will then perish.
Next, the mantra of the Heart of Hearts (Cittacittavidhi) is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ sṭri-kāra-lumpa hūṃ khaṃ svāhā. When performing this rite, one should recite it in this manner.
Recite this heart mantra while sealing the five places of the body;
it is used for protecting oneself, expelling obstructors, and establishing the boundary.
If one can recite it one thousand times every day, no evil persons or enemies will find an opportunity to cause harm.
It causes those who commit evil deeds to fail in their aims;
curses and incantations are all utterly destroyed. If one sees an evil dream, reciting this seven times shall cause the evil dream not to manifest.
Furthermore, there is a method for binding the Heart-to-Heart Seal (Citta-cittā-mudrā).
Waving [the hand] from afar toward the direction of Setodhruva,
if calamities arise within one's household or nation— such as epidemics, droughts, or floods—
one should generate a heart of great compassion if one wishes to dispel them.
Contemplating from afar that the people within those realms give rise to mutual compassion toward one another—
regarding each other as fathers, mothers, sons, or daughters—
one shall immediately have calamities extinguished by reciting the mantra ten thousand times.
Next is the method for binding the fundamental mudrā:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward to form fists;
extend the two middle fingers straight upward.
When the heads are joined together, it is completed.
This mudrā possesses great power and great divine efficacy;
as soon as one forms this mudrā and recites the mantra...
That person is identical to the body of the Great Majestic Wrathful Vidyārāja, without any difference.
Next, the method for the heart-seal (hṛdayamudrā) is explained:
it is the same as the root seal mentioned previously.
Extend the two index fingers and bend them like a trident; thus the seal is formed.
Having bound this seal, recite the mantra.
All ritual activities and dharmas will be accomplished.
Next, the Heart-to-Heart Mudrā is explained;
it is the same as the previous Heart Mudrā.
By simply holding up the two index fingers, the seal is formed.
By binding this seal and reciting the mantra,
one can accomplish all tasks.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to crush an enemy,
one should construct a triangular mandala and paint the Great Majestic Vidyārāja within it.
The body is the color of a dark cloud,
with flames arising from every part of it,
and it wields various colored weapons.
Regarding the three characters for "peace of body":
this means placing the syllable Oṃ at the crown of the head and the syllable Aḥ at the mouth.
The mind is established as the syllable HŪṂ.
Once the body of the Honored One has been accomplished,
place various śatadruḥs beneath the image and set down the name.
Before this image,
one should arrange oneself within the same maṇḍala according to the ritual methods for images;
the majestic efficacy shall be exactly like this.
Immediately form the mudrā and recite the aforementioned Great Heart Mantra one thousand and eighty times.
Within the phrases and meanings of the mantra, omit the syllable *turu* and call out the person's name.
This will cause that host to naturally retreat and disperse,
or it will cause them to become severely ill, vomit blood, and perish.
Furthermore, one should paint their image and visualize oneself [as the deity].
He is blue-black in color,
with six feet, six heads, and six arms.
Thus he purifies the six realms of existence, fulfills the six perfections, and accomplishes the six supernormal powers.
Next, recite the Three-Syllable Vidya and, at each respective location, arrange the mantra, saying:
Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ. Having thus performed this empowerment and accomplished the body, one then recites the praise to the Great Majestic King Vidyārāja.

*Namo varadavajragarbha mañjughoṣa mahā-māra-saha-sarva-vighna-vijaye vijñāna-raśmi-padmāṅka.* Next, the twenty-three kinds of offerings that cause the rites to be performed to be swiftly accomplished shall be explained.
Next, the mantra for following the mind is:
Oṃ śrīkaraṇadā hūṃ khaṃ svāhā. Next, the mantras for the heart, the crown, and the mouth-heart are as follows:
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ. First, form the mudrā and recite while visualizing these three syllables;
they become blue and manifest as the principal deity.
He has six feet, six heads, and six arms.

To purify the six realms of existence, fulfill the six perfections, and accomplish the six supernormal powers, the ritual for the recitation of the Noble Wrathful King Yamāntaka is next explained; first, the summary verse (*uddāna*) states: [The twenty-three kinds of offerings]...
First, from sweeping the ground and reciting, Next, the invitation,
the *argha* offering, the seat, the bath, the bell, The robe, the unguents, the incense, the flowers,
and the empowerment with five-colored powders; One surrounds the mandala and recites the mantra.
Next, recite the mantras for the jeweled banners and pennants,
the jeweled chariots, jeweled pavilions, fans, and various ornaments; offer the lamps, the food,
and the count of recitations, and finally perform the ritual of sending forth the Buddha.
Having completed the recitation, follow the painted image; in this sequence, all is thus.
This verse is a secret for the wise; the practitioner of recitation should know it for himself.
The mantra is as follows: [it consists of] twenty-three syllables.
Now, beginning with the sweeping of the ground, the mantra for sweeping is:
Oṃ jñapti-mata mata sarvabuddhān. The mantra for summoning is as follows:

Oṃ (1) kṣamukha (2) kṣapuja (3) kṣarāṇa (4) ātumuśala (5) paraśupāśahasta arghya-mantra: [The mantra for the water-offering (*arghya*) is as follows:]... [mantra continues] ... *arghyam pratīccha svāhā*.

Oṃ sarvabuddha-pāyātaka-vajra-ghaṇṭā-mantra: Oṃ aṭṭaṭṭaha-sannini hūṃ phaṭ.
The mantra for the offering of the garment: Oṃ vastra-hūṃ.
Oṃ vighnarāja-maṇivāsana; the mantra for incense is: Oṃ kuru kuru sarvakarmāṇi.
The mantra for burning incense is: [Oṃ kuru kuru sarvakarmāṇi].
The mantra for *oṃ cina cina sarvamantra* (the Flower Mantra) is:
*Oṃ cina cina paramudraṇa*. The mantra for empowering the five-colored powders to encircle the maṇḍala is: [as above].
Oṃ sarva-uṣṇīṣa-praveśaya praveśaya maṇḍala-maṭhe. This is the mantra for the precious canopy.
Oṃ ma-vilamba ma-vilamba. The mantra for the banner and pennant is:
Oṃ vighasāda-vidantakara. The mantra for the pennant is: [Oṃ vighasāda-vidantakara].
Oṃ kuru kuru mama kāryāṇi. The mantra of the Jewel Canopy (Ratnavitāna) is:
Oṃ sarvaśapariplāvaka. The mantra of the Jewel Pavilion (Ratnakūṭa) is: Oṃ.
Oṃ samayam anusmara śānti mantra: Oṃ sphoṭaya sphoṭaya. The mantra for adornment: Oṃ sphoṭaya sphoṭaya.
Oṃ ākarṣaya ākarṣaya. The lamp mantra is: Oṃ nahā nahā paca paca. The food offering mantra is: Oṃ.
Oṃ kha kha khāhi khāhi naṣṭa-sattvānāṃ mārga-darśaka. The mantra for the number of recitations is as follows:
The mantra for sending off Brahmā is: Oṃ khe khe brahmaṇe svāhā.
The mantra for the *Kiñjalka* [deity] is: Oṃ kiñjalkāya svāhā.
The mantra for the *Vikṛtānana* [deity] is: Oṃ vikṛtānana svāhā. The above are the mantras.
If the practitioner recites this three or seven times,
they will possess the twenty-three kinds of offerings mentioned above;
whatever *siddhi* they seek will be swiftly accomplished.
Furthermore, among the twenty-three kinds of vidyās mentioned above,
one should empower the five-colored powders with the vidyā;
once the mandala has been established, [one should proceed].
One should empower the powder with this mantra and use it to encircle the maṇḍala.
Once the recitation of the dismissal mantra is completed and one wishes to depart from the ritual enclosure (maṇḍala), [one should proceed].
One should recite this vidyā to dismiss the assembly of noble ones.
Furthermore, if one wishes for the noble ones to descend swiftly, to quickly eliminate obstacles and difficulties,
and to fulfill their original vows, [one should proceed as follows].
Following the previous instructions, construct a triangular fire altar.
One should take guggulu incense and white mustard seeds, mix them with mānuṣa-rudhira (human blood),
various poisons, red mustard seeds, and oil.
Take one hundred and eight single-stemmed leaves and one hundred and eight branches of *kṛtavedhana*,
sharpening both ends to a point twelve finger-widths long.
Use these to apply oil while reciting the mantra as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām | apratihataśāsanānām | tadyathā | he he mahākrodha | śamukha | śambhuja | śaṃkarana | sarva...
Vīṇāgaṇḍaka hūṃ hūṃ kiñjalka-ye simahāvīṇāya ka | dvīndraka-ra no svābhāna-mi-nāśaya lahu lahu samayam || 7–10 ||
*Ṇa-sma-ra sa-phaṭ sa-phaṭ ṭha (with a half-syllable *ṭha*, as above) svāhā*. Having recited this once:
Then, cast various incense and medicinal herbs into the fire one hundred and eight times.
Once all one hundred and eight pieces have been offered,
whatever vow you seek shall be fully accomplished.
At that time, the Noble One did not violate his original vow;
he swiftly arrived at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) to provide his protective empowerment.
If there were any evil dreams, through the power of this empowerment, they would all cease to appear and be ultimately extinguished.
Once the practitioner has completed the preceding recitations of all these dharmas within the maṇḍala,
they should exit the maṇḍala and give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and compassion, refraining from thoughts of resentment or harm.
They may then walk at will and freely recite or read Mahāyāna sūtras.
The Ritual for the Recitation of the Greatly Efficacious and Accomplished Mantra of the Holy Wrathful King Yamāntaka.
